prompts.title: Body rebuild
prompts.text:
LIMEN — accepted v2 body rebuild specification, A-pose references added 19 October 2026.
This is a reusable brief, not a transcript of the original Meshy task. Attach the three supplied body images whose filenames start limen-apose-front, limen-apose-back and limen-apose-side as views of ONE character. Use front as the primary input and rear/side as supporting views. They are orthographic renders of the same accepted v2 body in its neutral A-pose, with identical framing and the approved pale-steel palette. Preserve these proportions and construction. The Set 1 character concept sheet is reference only for identity/material intent; do not upload its multi-character collage as the body or combine the separate clipboard with it.

Create LIMEN, Loopforge's security chief: broad heavy worn industrial armour, recognizable helmet and cyan optics, dark mechanical joints, legible chest insignia and robust planted feet. Preserve the original Set 1 skull face, armour anatomy and silhouette. Follow the owner-approved 19 October concept palette: pale steel armour (direction #AAB9BD), dark mechanical recesses, deeper saturated teal-cyan optics and energy. No machine gun. The horizontal protocol clipboard shown beside the body is a separate equipment concept: do not fuse it into the body. Neutral symmetric A-pose, hands clear of torso, two separated legs. Full humanoid body with useful hands. No blade or energy fused to the body, hand, leg or torso.

Keep high-detail master separately. Produce a roughly 41–43k-triangle delivery candidate without losing helmet, joints, hands or silhouette. The accepted v2 had 42,354 triangles; a new generation need not reproduce its topology. Preserve available PBR texture maps; target 2K working maps and no baked glow halo. Do not claim maps, rigid weights or finger bones that are absent.

Export unrigged neutral GLB and editable FBX. Inspect front/back/profile before rigging. Retain the exact accepted source if shape changes are unnecessary: animation cleanup alone is not a reason to regenerate the body.

prompts.title: Emitter rebuild
prompts.text:
LIMEN — separate rigid forearm emitter
Use the accepted body and original cyan blade reference. Generate the physical emitter housing and forearm mounting collar as ONE rigid separate accessory, with its longitudinal axis and mounting end clearly identified. Do not generate a hand, arm, body, floor or background. The complete source blade may include energy geometry, but our runtime retains the housing and creates the energy procedurally; prefer the physical housing alone for this rebuild.

Preserve dark worn metal, cyan-adjacent accents, engineered vents and attachment details. Target about 5,000 triangles for the delivery housing, keeping the high-resolution master separate. Export textured GLB and editable FBX with actual dimensions, axes and material inventory. No skeleton is required for a rigid attachment.

Mounting offsets, scale and handedness will be fitted to LIMEN's right forearm offline. Do not claim clearance from a standalone prop. We will validate walk, run, maintenance idle, blends and worker contacts after assembly.

The current 672-triangle core and braids, rapid energy flow, independent cyan/jade/blue/violet shifts, flicker/power-down/restart, reduced-effects mode and future sparks are authored in the renderer. Do not bake those effects into a heavy Meshy mesh.

prompts.title: Rig and delivery
prompts.text:
Rig the approved blade-free LIMEN body as a humanoid with Mixamo-compatible export naming. Preserve a neutral rigged A-pose and the same mesh/materials for each clip. Include walking and running takes with original names, durations and root travel documented. Export GLB with Rigged Character enabled, embedded textures, and every selected animation; export individual clips if the combined file omits any. Supply FBX for offline cleanup.

The accepted v2 source has 23 joints and no articulated fingers; do not assume a new rig shares those transforms. Report actual bones, skin weights, maps and embedded clips. Preserve original downloads and source hashes.

The 11-second emitter-adjustment idle is our offline-authored animation: planted stance, raise emitter, inspect, power down, opposite hand adjusts housing, two restart attempts, reignite, lower arm. It is not a Meshy catalog clip. Refit/rebake it for any changed skeleton or socket. Keep a separate authored derivative and compare against source. Avoid a global arm offset that breaks other motions.

Before adoption: validate neutral pose, walks/runs, full-cycle blade/body/floor clearance, material appearance, factory CCTV recognition and actual performance. The existing source-specific import recipe and socket calibration are not automatically valid for a regenerated model.

prompts.title: Stage 6 · Doorway step back
prompts.text:
LIMEN — DOORWAY AVOIDANCE
21 October 2026. Keep the accepted body, cyan blade and existing motion bank.

Source: downloaded Meshy_AI_LIMEN_security_chief_biped_Step_Back.zip. Embedded Step_Back duration 0.833333 s; imported by matching source bone names, retaining the other 17 clips. Catalog ID was not supplied and must not be invented. Source archive SHA-256 f73c741193bf78f6695329bd28cd25d0157efeaf514f108ed6b2d399a6b91afe.

After two completed worker ID checks, STILETTO marches through the main door and Security using the accepted Quick Walk. Fit LIMEN's Step_Back to clear her approaching torso and both blades, facing her. She does not slow or stop. Review the source's airborne/foot-contact timing; if a stronger hop is needed, tune or acquire it rather than claim this export already supplies the whole action. Turn back towards the workers and return to the threshold after she passes. The workers retreat on individual paths, with bob protecting his injured leg.

Validate the complete contact envelope, planted feet, root motion and entry/exit blends in close-up and the held doorway composition. Do not change accepted supervisor appearance or replace the cyan blade with a baton. Store any correction as a separate derivative with source hash, constraints and review evidence.

prompts.title: Stage 7 · Checkpoint cyan strike
prompts.text:
LIMEN — checkpoint strike, motion audition

Use the existing accepted LIMEN body, pale steel finish and RIGHT forearm cyan blade. Do not regenerate the body or change the rig.

The beat: bob takes one step through the checkpoint without permission. LIMEN makes one sharp, deliberate right-arm slash, catches bob across the upper body, then resumes control of the doorway. This is a punishment, not a prolonged combat routine. Left hand stays clear of the blade. No two-handed axe grip, full-body spin or repeated combo.

Catalog candidate: Action 219, Right_Hand_Sword_Slash. Audition the motion on an existing API rig, transfer its body-space joint rotations onto the accepted LIMEN rig, then adjust stance, blade contact and exit pose against bob. Keep the source take and the fitted performance separately reviewable. One source animation request: 3 Meshy credits within the existing 500-credit opening budget.

Acceptance: visible anticipation, one readable contact, bob reacts at that contact, blade clears LIMEN and witnesses, feet remain planted except the intended step. Review from the beside-bob shot and the room camera. Preserve uninterrupted STILETTO passage later in the scene.

prompts.title: 08 · Landing supervisor rebuild
prompts.text:
LIMEN — landing supervisor body revision, 21 October 2026

Reason: the opening scene uses a lower-detail animation-delivery body that loses the exposed skull, strong plate shapes and forearm energy silhouette. The owner authorized regeneration; previous model and palette approval do not constrain this revision. Pale steel serves shot contrast, not an all-over white finish.

Input: limen-skull-front-v3.png. Generated from the approved Set 1 pale-steel concept sheet and the original LIMEN Security interaction art. Single body, symmetric A-pose, both hands, no attached prop. Identity: exposed mechanical skull and teeth, heavy brow, bright cyan eye sockets, cable neck, broad shoulders, large chest/name plate, substantial boots. The right forearm has a compact mount only. No weapon geometry fused into the body.

Generate a textured 30k-triangle candidate, preserve the higher-resolution source, export GLB with 2K PBR. Keep broad pale/mid-steel plate faces separated by deep charcoal joints. Avoid camouflage and dense mottling that collapse at room scale. Inspect front, rear and profile before rigging. Reuse and retarget the existing motion library after validating bind pose and bone mapping; do not assume prior fixes survive a new mesh.

Keep the cyan blade separate. Fit its mount to the forearm and preserve a broad, flowing, unmistakable blade silhouette in the greeting and strike shots. Inspect eyes, skull and energy shape at room and console scale. Compare with actual Lobby/Security floors and illumination. This is a candidate until those views, animation contacts and performance are checked.
